title: SGLT2 Inhibitors in Heart Failure Regardless of Diabetes
summary: SGLT2 inhibitors reduce heart failure hospitalizations and cardiovascular death across the EF spectrum independent of diabetes. Benefits emerge within weeks, with consistent safety signals and modest eGFR dip. Incorporate dapagliflozin or empagliflozin as foundational therapy for HFrEF and as additive therapy for HFmrEF/HFpEF.
clinicalQuestion: In adults with heart failure (any EF), should SGLT2 inhibitors be used regardless of type 2 diabetes status?

keyMoments.title: Class effect across EF and diabetes status
keyMoments.body: SGLT2 inhibitors **reduce HHF and CV death across HFrEF and HFpEF**, **independent of diabetes** status, with early separation of event curves [1], [2], [3], [4].

keyMoments.title: Rapid symptom and quality-of-life gains
keyMoments.body: KCCQ scores improve within weeks; meaningful benefits observed by 12 weeks in HFrEF and HFpEF cohorts [2], [3], [4].

keyMoments.title: Consistent safety profile
keyMoments.body: Adverse events include **genital mycotic infections** and an **initial eGFR dip**; **DKA and severe hypoglycemia are rare** in nondiabetics [1], [2], [3], [4].

keyMoments.title: Renal protection signal
keyMoments.body: Slower eGFR decline and reduced renal events observed, especially in HFrEF; attenuated but present in HFpEF [1], [3], [4].

sections.title: Implementing SGLT2 Inhibitors in Heart Failure
sections.blurb: Select dapagliflozin 10 mg or empagliflozin 10 mg once daily for most patients with heart failure irrespective of diabetes.

steps.title: Initiate early in HFrEF
steps.body: Start **dapagliflozin 10 mg** or **empagliflozin 10 mg** in all symptomatic HFrEF (NYHA II–IV) unless contraindicated; benefit on **CV death/HHF: HR ~0.74–0.75** with effect **independent of diabetes** [1], [2].

steps.title: Add in HFmrEF/HFpEF
steps.body: Use SGLT2 inhibitors to reduce **HHF** and improve symptoms in HFmrEF/HFpEF; **HR 0.79** for composite CV death/HHF in both **EMPEROR-Preserved** and **DELIVER**, consistent in those without diabetes [3], [4].

steps.title: Renal thresholds and monitoring
steps.body: Initiate down to **eGFR ≥20–25 mL/min/1.73 m²** (agent-specific); expect a **transient eGFR fall (3–5 mL/min)**; monitor renal function and volume status 1–4 weeks after start [1], [3], [4].

steps.title: Volume and concomitant therapy
steps.body: Assess for hypovolemia; consider loop diuretic down-titration if euvolemic. Compatible with **ARNI/ACEI/ARB, beta-blocker, MRA**, and **GLP-1** agents; no uptitration required [2], [4].

steps.title: Peri-illness and procedure guidance
steps.body: Hold during acute illness, perioperatively, or if poor oral intake to mitigate rare **euglycemic DKA**; restart once stable [1], [2].

sections.title: Eligibility, Safety, and Follow-up
sections.blurb: Screen for candidacy and mitigate predictable adverse effects.

cards.title: Who is eligible?
items: HFmrEF/HFpEF (LVEF >40%): reduction in HHF and symptom gains [3], [4]
With or without type 2 diabetes; not for type 1 diabetes due to DKA risk [1], [2]

cards.title: When to avoid or pause
items: Active DKA or history of euglycemic DKA [1], [2]
Severe volume depletion or hypotension; correct before initiation [2], [4]
Recurrent genital mycotic infections; counsel and consider prophylaxis [1], [3]

cards.title: Baseline labs and targets
items: BMP, eGFR, potassium; A1c if diabetes status unknown
Expect initial creatinine rise ≤30% from baseline; recheck in 1–4 weeks [1], [3]
Urinalysis not required for initiation; proteinuria does not contraindicate

cards.title: Follow-up milestones
items: Assess symptoms and BP at 2–4 weeks; review weight and diuretic needs
Renal function and electrolytes at 1–4 weeks, then every 3–6 months
Reinforce sick-day rules; pause for surgery or severe illness

cards.title: Key benefits to discuss
items: HFrEF: fewer HHF and CV deaths (HR ~0.74–0.75) [1], [2]
HFpEF/HFmrEF: fewer HHF (HR 0.79) and better KCCQ scores [3], [4]
Renal protection: slower eGFR decline; fewer serious renal events in HFrEF [1]

cards.title: Adverse effects and mitigation
items: Genital mycotic infections: hygiene counseling; topical azoles if needed [1], [2]
Volume depletion/dizziness: adjust diuretics; encourage fluids if safe [2], [4]
Rare euglycemic DKA: hold during acute illness; consider ketone testing if symptomatic [1]
